checks: The fixed-mass finite box is compact. A mass exchange from an occupied smaller site to an unfilled larger site strictly improves the first moment, proving that the maximizing selection fills in descending order with at most one partial site.

If p=P(Z>=1) is at least theta, the retained top mass lies on integers >=1, and any site >1 contributes positively to the top selection, forcing strictness. If p<theta, the excluded bottom mass lies on integers <=0. Any negative site then contributes strictly negative excluded first moment. The complementary moment argument includes possible partial mass at zero.

For min support 0 the mean forces p<=theta; if p=theta every positive site is one. For max support 1 the mean forces p>=theta. Since the mean is strictly between integers, minimum and maximum support lie on opposite sides of it; these cases prove the exact union and cover the tie p=theta.

A constant theta density has selected mass theta and first moment theta squared. In the strict case the stated coefficient is in (0,1); the combined density is bounded below by (1-lambda)theta and above by 1-(1-lambda)(1-theta), both strict.

Independent rational checks: on {0,2} of weights (3/4,1/4), on {-1,1} of weights (1/4,3/4), and on {0,1} with equal weights, theta=U=1/2. The four-site uniform law on {-1,0,1,2} gives U=3/4 at theta=1/2 and mixed densities (1/4,1/4,3/4,3/4), of both mass and moment 1/2.

The source 461e51dc31c626f1 §1 gives this marginal theorem with the same equality alternatives. The uniformly fractional conclusion is the explicit formula of §2 applied only when both extremes extend past the adjacent pair.
